page.layout: One printed page, the right-hand page of the opening. Top: a woodcut headpiece (not text). Then a centred title block of three lines: "THESES THEOLOGICÆ / DE / SACRAMENTIS / IN GENERE." Below it, the running text in one column, with a large woodcut initial D. No marginal notes on this page. The left strip of the scan is the edge of the facing page and is not transcribed. The faint text at the top is show-through from the back of the leaf.

main_text.head: THESES THEOLOGICÆ DE SACRAMENTIS IN GENERE.
main_text.p: DEus ab initio Mundi non tantùm foederis & reconciliationis doctrinam Ecclesiæ tradidit: verùm etiam ritus externos promissionibus additos obseruari iussit, qui sunt alterum fidei nostræ adminiculum, & Latinè Sacramenta nuncupantur: quæ vox licet sit ἀ̓γέαφος[?], tamen Sacræ Scripturæ non aduersatur, sed respondet Græcè μυστήριον. In præsenti verò συζητήσει[?] & in quem finem instituta fuerint Sacramenta, & quis nunc eorum sit usus, σὺν θεῷ, demonstrabimus.
Verùm, ut hoc ordine perficiatur, primo lo-co vocabuli notio, deinde rei definitio consideran-da est.
Vox Sacramenti à sacro dicta duo habet significa-ta, primò significat solenne iusiurandum, quod non nisi inuocato numine concipiebatur: hinc nata est

page.notes: The woodcut headpiece and the woodcut initial D are decorations, not text. The "Thesis I." label, and the numbers "II." and "III.", are written as paragraphs because they are numbered theses or bare numbers. The Greek word after "Ecclesiæ tradidit" in the first paragraph is hard to read; I have marked it [?]. "συζητήσει" is also uncertain at the initial letters. The line-end hyphens in "lo-co", "consideran-da" and "significa-ta" are printed hyphens and are kept. The running head is not transcribed because the only text at the top is show-through from the other side. The printed number is the gathering signature "A 2", so there is no separate page number.
